label: Skilled's keyed lookup performs no staleness check: loadIndex reads and parses one artifact, lookup scores and sorts, and exit 1 means no result scored above zero, with no git call, mtime comparison or freshness import.

A single definition of staleness already exists in lib/freshness.mjs (phrase-set difference) and is consumed by generate-trigger-index --check and by the save path's checkTriggerIndexFreshness; the lookup is the one consumer that does not use it.
The failure is live: zero of the index's 17,653 paths match the new packet 002-retrieval-lessons-research, and both the unscoped and the packet-scoped topic queries exited 1 with zero results.

Corpus-wide staleness is tiny (39 of 67,595 spec md files newer than the 11:58 index, 0.06 percent) but concentrated on the newest packets, which are the likely subject of a fresh session's first prompt.

The committed index has no build timestamp (top-level keys are manifestHash, normalization, paths, phrases, schemaVersion), so sweet-search's publishedAt-versus-mtime freshness rule cannot be ported, and checkout mtime is untrustworthy in a worktree clone.

Fallback cost is scoped: repo-wide changed list 0.88-0.90s versus cold lookup 0.07s (about 13x), packet-scoped git call 0.02-0.03s, rev-parse guard 0.01s, frontmatter read and match of the 15 changed md files 0.02s.

label: The scan target does not transfer: sweet-search greps body content over a sparse-gram index, while Skilled's keyed lane answers declared trigger_phrases, so the fallback must read frontmatter and score with scorePhrase rather than grep prose.

A git-aware fallback creates a contract tension with conventions section 5's promise that two runs over an unchanged corpus produce the same ordering, so the build phase must amend the claim and add an explicit marker and opt-out.
generate-trigger-index --check already reports this staleness but costs one full corpus walk and is documented as running in advisory CI and by hand, never per lookup.
A five-prompt probe plus the two topic queries produced 2 of 7 zero-hits, so zero-hits are the minority of ordinary prompts but the norm for genuinely new topics; the sample is a probe, not a rate.

label: Staleness has exactly one definition in Skilled, the phrase-set difference in lib/freshness.mjs; any fallback must reuse it rather than introduce a second definition.
Outside a git work tree there is no changed-file list, so the fallback must do nothing rather than guess.
